text: Multidisciplinary tumor board for 62F with stage IV colorectal cancer with liver metastases. ATTENDEES: Medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiation oncology, radiology, pathology, hepatobiliary surgery. PRESENTATION: MSS colorectal cancer, KRAS G12D mutant, with limited liver metastases (2 lesions). Primary tumor is symptomatic with anemia and near-obstruction. Performance status ECOG 1. DISCUSSION: Patient not candidate for anti-EGFR therapy due to KRAS mutation. Liver metastases potentially resectable if good response to chemotherapy. Primary tumor symptomatic and may require intervention. OPTIONS: (1) Upfront chemotherapy with FOLFOX + bevacizumab, reassess for resection. (2) Primary tumor resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. (3) Diverting colostomy followed by chemotherapy. RECOMMENDATION: Given symptomatic primary with risk of obstruction, recommend primary tumor resection with concurrent liver metastasectomy if technically feasible, followed by adjuvant FOLFOX + bevacizumab. If liver lesions not resectable at time of surgery, proceed with colectomy alone and adjuvant chemotherapy. Patient agrees with surgical approach.
